name: Brotherhood's End
summary: In Stormwind Keep, Lord Gregor Lescovar's killing leaves dangerous questions behind. Master Mathias Shaw sends you to City Architect Baros Alexston and warns you to keep the killer's identity quiet.

sections.title: Loose Ends in the Shadows
sections.body: After Lord Gregor Lescovar and his Defias contact, Marzon the Silent Blade, are killed, Master Mathias Shaw urges caution. Killing a high-ranking noble inside the royal keep risks political trouble, even though Lescovar was deep in treason. Shaw tells you to share the broad strokes of the Defias conspiracy with Baros Alexston. Keep your own part in the killing, and the rogue cheese merchant Elling Trias's involvement, off the record.

sections.title: A Breath of Relief
sections.body: Baros Alexston, the City Architect who helped rebuild Stormwind as a stonemason, is relieved to hear that Lescovar is dead. Edwin VanCleef had marked Alexston and other prominent figures in the rebuilding effort for vengeance after the Stonemasons were cast out without pay. With Lescovar silenced and the conspiracy disrupted, Alexston believes the immediate threat to the kingdom's architects and nobility has passed.

faq.answer: After killing Lord Gregor Lescovar in Stormwind Keep, you report to Master Mathias Shaw at SI:7. Shaw sends you to City Architect Baros Alexston, who wants to know whether the Defias plot against the city's leaders has been foiled.

faq.q: Why does Shaw tell you not to admit to killing Lescovar?
faq.answer: Lord Gregor Lescovar was a high nobleman in Stormwind's House of Nobles. Though he was proven to collude with the Defias, admitting to his assassination in the royal keep could bring political scandal and scrutiny. Shaw advises leaving the deed unattributed.

faq.q: Why should nobody mention Elling Trias?
faq.answer: Elling Trias poses as a cheese merchant in the Trade District, but he is a veteran operative with many contacts in the city's shadows. Revealing his part in uncovering the conspiracy could expose his cover and compromise his underground network.

faq.q: Why was Baros Alexston personally concerned about the Defias?
faq.answer: Baros Alexston belonged to the Stonemasons Guild and helped rebuild Stormwind alongside Edwin VanCleef. When the House of Nobles refused to pay the workers, the masons turned to banditry. Alexston stayed in the city's service and became a target of VanCleef's revenge.

faq.q: Does this quest mark the end of the Defias threat?
faq.answer: Killing Edwin VanCleef's key sympathizer in the House of Nobles does not erase the Defias presence. But removing Lescovar deals a critical blow to their efforts inside Stormwind's government and averts an immediate coup within the city walls.

faq.q: Where does this investigation lead next?
faq.answer: Relieved by your success against the conspirators, Baros Alexston prepares a report on the Defias Brotherhood for the King. He asks you to deliver it at an audience in Stormwind Keep, in An Audience with the King.

angles.text: Uncovering the Defias conspiracy inside Stormwind Keep shows that the kingdom faces subversion from within its noble halls as well as from bandits across the countryside.
Mathias Shaw's warning reflects SI:7's unspoken rule: deliver the kingdom's justice in silence, without taking public credit for a noble's blood.
For humans of Stormwind, this assignment closes the loop on the Stonemasons' rebellion that began in the city's streets years ago, securing justice without tearing the kingdom apart.
